To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

family social environments are important determinants of health and disease across the life span, and that family social environments represent vital links in understanding health and disease across time.

(a) family environments are important for the development of mental health and physical health, (b) family environments are characterized by conflict, aggression, coldness, and neglect, and (c) these family environments are associated with poor health and early mortality.

the family social environment, including family conflict and aggression and family warmth and support, is a major influence on mental and physical health, and that this influence operates through the development of emotion processing and social competencies, biological stress response systems, and health behaviors, especially the use of substances.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the family environment in the development of psychopathology and physical health problems in children and adults.
the interplay between the social and biological processes in the etiology and course of mental and physical health.
the interplay of genetic and social factors that contribute to mental and physical health in children and adults.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the family environment is the primary socialization context for children.

the quality of family social environments has profound and enduring influences on the health of offspring across the life span and that the mechanisms by which these effects are produced are biobehaviorally based.
family characteristics and family relationships are important determinants of health and disease in offspring.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the family is the most important environmental influence on health and well-being, and that the family represents a key target of intervention and prevention.

risky families are characterized by a constellation of family processes that create a toxic environment for children, and that this environment leads to a cascade of adverse outcomes for children and adolescents.
the family is the crucible in which the seeds of mental and physical health are sown.
The main takeaway from our work is that
family social environment represents a critical factor for the development of health and disease.
we need to focus on the family, and especially the mother, as a critical context for understanding the development of health and illness across the life span.
the social environment of the family is a powerful force in shaping children's health and well being.
